sections.title: Letter sound of R
paragraphs: The letter is called (R) /ɑːr/. Its main sound is heard in the word (red) /rɛd/, a colour. This letter has two main variants in English pronunciation. In some positions the voice sounds clearly. In other positions the letter can become completely silent.

sections.title: How to pronounce R
paragraphs: To make the first sound, curl your tongue tip back behind the teeth ridge. Do not touch the roof of your mouth. Round your lips slightly and let the air flow smoothly. This sound is voiced. Touch your throat to feel it shake. For the silent variant, make no sound and keep your tongue still.

sections.title: Spelling rules for R
paragraphs: Before a vowel sound, pronounce this letter as heard in (run) /rʌn/. At the end of a syllable or word, many speakers make it a silent letter. You can hear this quiet ending in (car) /kɑː/. The letter also stays silent before another consonant, as heard in (hard) /hɑːd/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with R
paragraphs: Do not tap your tongue against your teeth like the sound in Spanish pero. A tap is a consonant where the tongue touches one time, very fast. Do not roll your tongue like a trill. Keep the tongue tip curled back and floating. Make sure your tongue never touches the roof of your mouth.
